skill.name: vercel-deploy-claimable
skill.description: Deploy web projects to Vercel and return preview and claim links without requiring a Vercel login.
skill.summary: Deploy a web project to Vercel and return claimable deployment links.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick and URL findings are markdown code fences, inline code, or example links, so they are false positives. The usage examples still tell agents to run an external deployment script that is not included in the audited package. The deployment flow can upload project contents to Vercel, so it needs clearer safeguards before publication.

remediation.suggestion: Include deploy.sh in the skill package or remove the shell command until reviewers can inspect it.
Exclude .env files, keys, secrets, private configs, and large generated folders before packaging.
Ask for explicit user confirmation before uploading project contents to Vercel.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Packages your project into a tarball (excludes `node_modules` and `.git`)
- `path` - Directory to deploy, or a `.tgz` file (defaults to current directory)
The script auto-detects frameworks from `package.json`. Supported frameworks include:
For static HTML projects (no `package.json`), framework is set to `null`.
- If there's a single `.html` file not named `index.html`, it gets renamed automatically
- This ensures the page is served at the root URL (`/`)
- **Other Frontend**: Astro, Solid Start, Angular, Ember, Preact, Docusaurus

content.value_statement: Teams need fast preview deployments without setting up a Vercel account first. This skill guides deployment to Vercel and returns preview and claim links.
actual_capabilities: Documents packaging a project directory while excluding node_modules and .git.
Documents framework detection from package.json before deployment.
Provides shell command examples for deploying a project or tarball.
Documents live preview and claim URL output.
Describes static HTML handling when package.json is absent.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for Claude network egress settings.
limitations: The audited package does not include the referenced deploy.sh script.
Deployment requires network access to Vercel from the agent environment.
Sensitive files may be uploaded unless the deployment script excludes them.
The skill does not manage production domains, environment variables, or team settings.

use_cases.title: Preview a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Deploy a web app branch and share a live preview before merge.

use_cases.title: Share a Static Site
use_cases.description: Publish a static HTML project quickly for review by stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Hand Off a Deployment
use_cases.description: Create a claimable Vercel deployment that a client can transfer into their account.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy Current Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner deployment from the current workspace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this app to Vercel and show me the preview URL and claim URL.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy the project in ./apps/web to Vercel. Confirm the framework you detect before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Static Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy the static HTML site in ./dist to Vercel. Check that the root page will load correctly.

prompt_templates.title: Review Then Deploy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced deployment with a preflight check.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the project for secrets and generated files, then deploy only if the package looks safe. Report skipped files and deployment links.

output_examples.output: Deployment succeeded. The result includes a live preview link, a claim link, and the detected framework.
The static site was prepared and deployed. The response includes a preview link and a claim link for account transfer.

best_practices: Review the project for secrets before deployment.
Deploy previews before claiming the deployment in a production account.
Confirm the target directory so unrelated workspace files are not packaged.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy repositories that contain private credentials or customer data.
Do not use the claim URL as a public share link.
Do not assume the referenced shell script is safe without reviewing it.

faq.question: Does this require a Vercel account?
faq.answer: It can create a claimable deployment without authentication, but claiming the deployment requires a Vercel account.

faq.question: What links does it return?
faq.answer: It returns a preview link for the live site and a claim link for transferring ownership.

faq.question: Can it deploy static HTML?
faq.answer: Yes. It can handle projects without package.json and prepare a root page.

faq.question: Which frameworks can it detect?
faq.answer: It lists support for common React, Vue, Svelte, backend, and static site frameworks.

faq.question: What security checks should I do first?
faq.answer: Remove secrets, private data, and unnecessary files before deployment.

faq.question: Will it work when network access is restricted?
faq.answer: It may fail until Vercel domains are allowed in the agent environment.
